'''Thomas Lumley''' is an Australian statistician who serves as the chair of [[biostatistics]] at the [[University of Auckland]] in New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Levine|first=Marisa Taylor, Dan|date=2020-09-18|title=Pfizer vaccine trial bets on early win against coronavirus, documents show|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-usa-vaccines-idUSKBN26907S|access-date=2021-04-06}}</ref> Lumley is also a member of the "R Core Team."<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=R: Contributors|url=https://www.r-project.org/contributors.html|access-date=2021-04-06|website=www.r-project.org}}</ref>

He was elected as a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association|ASA]] (American Statistical Association) in 2012.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=ASA Fellows List|url=https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx|access-date=2021-04-06|website=www.amstat.org}}</ref> Lumley was also elected a fellow of the [[Royal Society Te Apārangi|Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 2015.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=View our current Fellows|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/view-our-fellows/|access-date=2021-04-06|website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref>

== Education ==
Lumley received his Bachelors of Science at [[Monash University]] in Melbourne, Australia in 1991,<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Thomas Lumley: CV|url=http://faculty.washington.edu/tlumley/cv.html|access-date=2021-04-06|website=faculty.washington.edu}}</ref> a Masters of Science in Applied Statistics at the [[University of Oxford]] in Oxford, United Kingdom in 1993,<ref name=":3" /> and his Ph.D. in  Biostatistics at the [[University of Washington]] in Seattle, Washington in 1998.<ref name=":3" />

== Work ==
Lumley is a professor of statistics at the University of Auckland where he  researches regression modelling, clinical trials, semiparametric inference, statistical computing, foundations, and genomics.<ref name=":3" /> His statistics publications are commonly cited in the statistics and biostatistics fields. He makes contributions to R as a member of the R Core Team<ref name=":0" /> and contributes to the StatsChat blog.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-05|title=Stats Chat|url=https://www.statschat.org.nz/|access-date=2021-04-06|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Awards ==

* Howard Hughes Medical Institute Predoctoral Fellowship from 1995 to 1998<ref name=":3" />
* Donovan J Thompson Award for Academic Excellence in Biostatistics in 1996<ref name=":3" />
* Best Oral Presentation at Biometric Society Student Paper Competition in 1997<ref name=":3" />
* Gertrude Cox Award for contributions to Statistical Practice in 2008<ref name=":3" />
* Elected as an ASA Fellow in 2012<ref name=":1" />
* Elected as a fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand in 2015<ref name=":2" />

== Notable works ==
Some of Lumley's notable publications from 2019 include:

* ''Estimating prediction error for complex samples''<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Holbrook|first1=Andrew|last2=Lumley|first2=Thomas|last3=Gillen|first3=Daniel|date=2020|title=Estimating prediction error for complex samples|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/cjs.11527|journal=Canadian Journal of Statistics|language=en|volume=48|issue=2|pages=204–221|doi=10.1002/cjs.11527|issn=1708-945X|arxiv=1711.04877|s2cid=55884368 }}</ref>
* ''Numerical evaluation of methods approximating the distribution of a large quadratic form in normal variables''<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Tong|last2=Lumley|first2=Thomas|date=2019-11-01|title=Numerical evaluation of methods approximating the distribution of a large quadratic form in normal variables|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167947319301136|journal=Computational Statistics & Data Analysis|language=en|volume=139|pages=75–81|doi=10.1016/j.csda.2019.05.002|s2cid=164691322 |issn=0167-9473|hdl=2292/48222|hdl-access=free}}</ref>
* ''Fast Generalized Linear Models by Database Sampling and One-Step Polishing''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lumley|first=Thomas|date=2019-10-02|title=Fast Generalized Linear Models by Database Sampling and One-Step Polishing|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/10618600.2019.1610312|journal=Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics|volume=28|issue=4|pages=1007–1010|doi=10.1080/10618600.2019.1610312|s2cid=54968117 |issn=1061-8600|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
